info.name: Order-Payment-API
info.description:
Order & Payment API (Laravel 12, JWT auth, simulated payments).

## Manual execution order
1. **Auth › Register** — creates the user (no auth required)
2. **Auth › Login** — stores the JWT automatically
3. **Orders › Create Order** — stores `order_id` automatically
4. **Orders › Update Order** (or the **Confirm Order** variant) — order must be `confirmed` before payment
5. **Payments › Process Payment (Success / Failure)** — stores `payment_id`
6. **Payments › List All Payments** / **List Order Payments**

## Delete Order
`DELETE /orders/{id}` is allowed **only for orders with zero payments** (any payment status blocks deletion → 409).
Use a separate paymentless order for the Delete example — never delete the paid order.

## Business rules
- Only `pending` orders can be updated (409 otherwise).
- Only `confirmed` orders can be paid (409 otherwise).
- Only one successful payment per order (retrying after success → 409).
- Retries after a failed payment are allowed.

All protected requests use Bearer authentication with the JWT captured from Login.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Unauthenticated endpoints. Register creates the user; Login returns the JWT used by every protected request.

exec: pm.test('Response contains message and user', function () {

request.description:
Registers a new user. Unauthenticated.

Rules: `name` required|max:255, `email` required|email|unique, `password` required|min:8|confirmed.

**201** returns `{message, user:{id,name,email}}` — the password is never returned.
**422** on validation errors (e.g. duplicate email).

response.name: 422 — Validation error (duplicate email)

request.description:
Authenticates with email/password against the JWT `api` guard and returns an access token.

The test script stores `access_token` into the `jwt_token` environment variable — only on success (2xx). Failed responses never overwrite stored variables.

**200** `{access_token, token_type:"bearer", expires_in}` (expires_in = JWT_TTL × 60 seconds).
**401** `{"message":"Invalid credentials."}`.
**429** when more than 5 login attempts are made within one minute from the same IP (if throttling is enabled on this environment).

response.name: 422 — Validation error

item.name: Orders
item.description: Order management. All endpoints require Bearer auth. Only the owner sees their own orders.

exec: pm.test('Order created with server-calculated total', function () {

request.description:
Creates an order with 1..n items. The total is calculated **server-side** (`Σ quantity × price`, exact BCMath decimal arithmetic) — any client-supplied `total`, `user_id` or `status` is ignored.

Rules: `customer_name` required|max:255, `customer_email` required|email, `items` required|array|min:1, each item `product_name` required|max:255, `quantity` required|integer|min:1|max:4294967295, `price` required|numeric|min:0|max:9999999999.99|≤2 decimals.

The aggregate total must fit decimal(12,2) (max `9999999999.99`) — otherwise **422**.

**201** returns `{message, order:{id,user_id,customer_name,customer_email,status:"pending",total,items:[]}}` and stores `order_id` in the environment.
**422** on validation errors. **401** without a valid token.

response.name: 422 — Validation error (aggregate total overflow)
422 — Validation error (price with 3 decimals)

query.description: Optional filter. Allowed: pending, confirmed, cancelled. Any other value → 422.

request.description:
Lists the authenticated user's orders, newest first, standard Laravel pagination (`per_page` 15).

Query: optional `status=pending|confirmed|cancelled` — invalid status → **422**.

**200** returns the paginator object: `data[]` (each with eager-loaded `items`), `current_page`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, `links`.

response.name: 422 — Invalid status filter

request.description:
Returns one of the authenticated user's orders with its items.

**404** for missing **or** foreign-owned order IDs (identical response — no existence leak). Malformed non-numeric IDs are not routed (404).

PATCH — partial update of a **pending** order.

All fields are optional (`sometimes|required`): `customer_name`, `customer_email`, `status` (`pending|confirmed|cancelled`), `items` (full replacement — old items are deleted, new items created, total recalculated server-side).

`total`, `user_id`, `order_id` are never accepted from the client.

**200** `{message, order:{...items}}`.
**409** `{"message":"Only pending orders can be updated."}` — confirmed/cancelled orders are immutable.
**422** on validation errors (rejected requests change nothing).
**404** missing/foreign order.

response.name: 409 — Only pending orders can be updated

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 OK and order confirmed', function () {

request.description:
Transitions a pending order to `confirmed` through the same PATCH endpoint — required before payment processing.

Allowed transitions from `pending`: `pending`, `confirmed`, `cancelled`. Once confirmed/cancelled, the order can never be modified again (409).

Run this **before** "Process Payment" in the workflow.

Deletes an order **only when it has zero payments** (any payment status — pending, successful, failed — blocks deletion with **409** `{"message":"Orders with payments cannot be deleted."}`). Deletion is independent of order status. Items are removed via DB cascade.

**204 No Content** — empty body.

⚠️ Set `paymentless_order_id` manually (create a separate order) — do **not** delete the paid `order_id`. Trying to delete a paid order returns 409 (see saved example).

item.name: Payments
item.description: Simulated payment processing. Only `confirmed` orders can be paid; one successful payment per order; retries allowed after failures.

request.description:
Processes a simulated payment via the configured gateway strategy.

- `method`: `credit_card` | `paypal` (validated against config/payment.php — disabled gateways → 422)
- `outcome`: `success` | `failure` — simulation control only, not a real gateway parameter

Both gateway outcomes return **201** because a Payment record is persisted (`status` = `successful` or `failed`).

**409** if the order is not `confirmed` (`"Only confirmed orders can be paid."`) or already has a successful payment (`"This order has already been paid."`).
**422** invalid method/outcome. **404** missing/foreign order. Stores `payment_id` in the environment on success.

response.name: 409 — Only confirmed orders can be paid
422 — Invalid method

exec: pm.test('Status is 201 Created (payment record stored as failed)', function () {

request.description:
Simulates a **failed** PayPal payment. Returns **201** because the Payment record is persisted with `status: "failed"`.

A retry (e.g. the Success variant) is allowed after a failure — failed payments never block new attempts.

Run the Success variant **after** this one to practice the retry flow. Only run one of them per order if you want a single successful payment.

exec: pm.test('Retry after failure succeeds with 201', function () {

request.description:
Retry flow: run after "Process Payment — Failure". A failed payment does not block new attempts; only a **successful** payment blocks (409).

This request replaces `payment_id` with the new successful payment's ID.

Lists all payments of the authenticated user's orders (across all orders), newest first, paginated (15).

**200** standard Laravel paginator JSON. Payments belonging to other users never appear.

Lists payments of one specific order belonging to the authenticated user, newest first, paginated (15).

**404** for missing or foreign-owned orders (identical response).
